(AP wire carried by ABC News; fetched 28 July 2026 evening)

France evacuates 4,000 more people as heat threatens wildfire fight across southwestern Europe (AP, 28 July 2026)

FRANCE / GIRONDE FIRE:
- ~4,000 people evacuated Tuesday from tourist sites on the Atlantic coast: campsites, holiday villages, tourist residences and leisure parks around the resort of Lacanau (incl. Lacanau Ocean and both shores of Lacanau lake). Precautionary.
- Gironde fire "stabilized, not fixed" — burned area unchanged at 420 sq km (162 sq miles).
- 220,000 previously evacuated in France due to the Gironde fire.
- 93 firefighters injured.
- France total 2026 burned: 1,160+ sq km (448+ sq miles).
- Forecast inland Gironde 33-35C (91-95F) from midday Tuesday; yellow heat warning for Gironde. Southeast winds inland, westerly sea breezes at coast.

QUOTES:
- Eric Brocardi, spokesperson, France's national firefighters federation: "We are at a point of fragility. We will continue attacking this fire despite the forecast rise in temperatures."
- President Emmanuel Macron: "The fire is fixed, which is good news in the Landes." (referring to the Landes area)

SPAIN:
- ~79,000 evacuated; 30,000 ordered to remain home (shelter in place).
- Ávila fire = Spain's largest wildfire on record, 500+ sq km (193+ sq miles).
- Spain total 2026 burned: 1,530 sq km (590 sq miles).
- Fourth heat wave expected; temperatures exceeding 40C (104F).

REGIONAL: France + Spain evacuations ~330,000 total.
